newsitem.title: FRANCE: Schneider sees 1997 big results increase.
newsitem.headline: Schneider sees 1997 big results increase.

text.p: The chairman of French electrical distribution company Schneider said on Wednesday he expected a "significant improvement" in 1997 results.

Didier Pineau-Valencienne told reporters, based on the first quarter of 1997, Schneider was forecasting average five percent growth for the year. "We are seeing the same trend as 1996, strong and unexpected growth in North America, also growth in emerging markets, South America, East Europe, Egypt," he said.
"The same trend for Germany and France, countries where we expect a recovery in industrial and property investment in the second half," he added.
He reiterated the group's aim of achieving a return on capital of 15 percent in the coming years, compared to a current 10.6 percent.
Schneider expected an "operating margin in constant progression" and that it was looking for 13 percent growth in its "Schneider 2000" plan to boost profitability, he said.
"This calls for time and effort but it is within our reach," he said at a presentation of the company's 1996 results.
Schneider earlier reported 1996 net attributable profit up 61.6 percent at 1.32 billion francs. The market consensus profit forecast was 1.25 billion francs.
